AlphaGenome in-silico shuffling of AP-1 (Fos) sites: cardiomyocyte arm

Generated 21 Oct 2026 · 3,679 cardiomyocyte Fos sites, 10 shuffle replicates per width · mouse heart ATAC track · fibroblast arm and MPRA still running

Main takeaways
  • What is solid. Shuffling the 170 bp around an AP-1 site removes far more predicted accessibility (median log2FC -1.75 in Stable sites) than shuffling the 11 bp motif alone (-0.61). This holds for essentially every site and is well above replicate noise.
  • Stable vs Dynamic is real. Stable sites depend more on their 170 bp context than Dynamic sites (+0.52, 95% CI +0.41 to +0.62). It survives adjustment for native accessibility and peak width, stratification by accessibility, a permutation test, and a second independent track (smaller there).
  • Age vs exercise vs combination. All dynamic classes behave alike. Comparing classes with each other (Age Up vs Down, Exercise Up vs Down) finds no differences at 170 bp or peak level. What separates classes is being stably bound or not, not the direction of change.
  • What is noise or unusable. RNA effects are about zero; AP-1 motif insertion into random backgrounds is at the floor; per-site peak-shuffle values scatter widely (replicate SD about 0.6) and are only trustworthy in aggregate.
  • Caveat on the slides. Our Dynamic-site native accessibility matches the slides closely, which suggests the pipeline reproduces the API, but our Stable-site set differs from the slides' (we could not reproduce their site counts). Absolute numbers should not be compared directly with the slides until the site set is resolved.

How to read this report

Effect. For each site and shuffle width, the effect is the mean over 10 shuffles of log2((shuffled + pc) / (native + pc)) of the predicted ATAC (mean per-base signal over a region; pc = 5% of the median native value). Negative = accessibility lost. A shuffle of the motif is read out over the motif, a 170 bp shuffle over the 170 bp, a peak shuffle over the peak ("matched readout"), unless stated.

Significance marks. *** FDR < 0.001, ** < 0.01, * < 0.05, ns not significant. Tests are two-sided Mann–Whitney against a reference class, Benjamini–Hochberg corrected within each family of tests. With thousands of sites a tiny difference is "significant", so each comparison also shows an effect size (difference of medians with a bootstrap 95% CI, and Cliff's delta: about 0.1 small, 0.3 medium, 0.5 large). Read the effect size before the stars.

Trust labels. ✓ Robust survives the checks below. ~ Plausible / partial real but small, or depends on a confound. ✗ Not supported no evidence, or indistinguishable from noise. ? Cannot judge yet data not available.

What it shows. The heart track predicts measured cardiomyocyte accessibility with a moderate rank correlation (the slides reported 0.49). The Patski (fibroblast-like) track is essentially uncorrelated with cardiomyocyte accessibility, as it should be. Trust: good enough to use the heart track as a proxy for cardiomyocyte sites; it is bulk heart tissue, not purified cardiomyocytes.

2. What does shuffling do?

What it shows. Shuffling only the motif lowers accessibility at the motif by about 0.6 log2 units (roughly a third lost) and over the whole peak by about 0.3 (about a fifth lost). Shuffling 170 bp or the whole peak is far more damaging (about -1.8 log2 units locally, i.e. around 70% lost). Dynamic sites lose less than Stable sites in most cells. Trust: the ordering motif < 170 bp ≈ peak is robust. Peak shuffles are noisy per site (see section 7).

3. Stable vs Dynamic: is the difference real?

Dynamic sites have lower native accessibility and different peak widths, either of which could make their log2FC look smaller without any biological difference. Three checks:

Native quintile Native ATAC (median) n Stable n Dynamic Stable median Dynamic median Dyn - Stable FDR sig.
1 0.08 511 225 -1.20 -0.95 0.25 3.6e-07 ***
2 0.16 550 186 -1.92 -1.62 0.30 7.4e-06 ***
3 0.26 589 146 -2.38 -1.73 0.66 1.0e-10 ***
4 0.45 623 113 -2.24 -1.56 0.68 9.7e-06 ***
5 0.97 634 102 -1.46 -0.57 0.89 3.2e-12 ***
  • Stratification: the gap is present in all five accessibility quintiles (all FDR < 0.05), so it is not a floor effect of low-accessibility sites.
  • Permutation test (5,000 label shuffles): 170 bp p = 0.0002, peak p = 0.0002, motif p = 0.091. The 170 bp and peak differences are far outside the null; the motif one is not.
  • Independent track: repeating the test with the Patski ATAC track on the same sites gives 170 bp +0.16 (**), peak -0.03 (ns), motif -0.00 (ns). The 170 bp direction replicates; the others do not.

Trust: robust for the 170 bp shuffle; partial for the peak shuffle; not supported for the motif shuffle.

4. Age, exercise and their combination

Each site carries three labels from the same binding calls: age class (YS vs MAS), exercise class (MAS vs MAE) and the full binding pattern. Every class is compared with its Stable reference, once raw and once adjusted for native ATAC and peak width (OLS with robust standard errors).

What it shows. At 170 bp every dynamic class loses about 0.45 to 0.6 log2FC less than Stable, and adjustment barely changes it. At the peak and motif widths, raw differences are small and the adjusted ones shrink toward zero. Between dynamic classes (the direct test of age vs exercise, and of up vs down):

Only the motif-width contrasts reach FDR < 0.05, with confidence intervals touching zero. There is no sign that age-driven and exercise-driven changes differ from each other in sequence dependence. Trust: "Stable vs dynamic" is robust; "which dynamic class" is not supported.

Positive peak-width coefficient: wider peaks lose less accessibility per log2FC. Dynamic sites differ systematically from Stable sites in width and native accessibility, which is why the raw peak-shuffle gap shrinks after adjustment.

5. RNA

What it shows. Predicted RNA barely moves when a distal AP-1 site or peak is shuffled (medians within about ±0.1), with the largest drops close to a TSS. ATAC and RNA effects correlate across sites (rho 0.19 to 0.24), so there is a weak coupling, but the RNA effects themselves are far smaller than the slides reported. Trust: not informative with these tracks; do not over-interpret.

What it shows. Effects get somewhat larger in the filtered sets (the model is more confident at accessible, well-predicted sites) and the Stable vs Dynamic gap at 170 bp stays. Trust: conclusions are not an artefact of poorly predicted sites; report all three tiers.

7. How much is noise?

Shuffle Median effect Median replicate SD Median SE (10 reps) Sites with |effect| > 2 SE Sites with effect < -2 SE
Motif (11 bp) -0.59 0.67 0.21 67% 60%
170 bp -1.63 0.31 0.10 94% 94%
Peak -1.21 0.62 0.20 80% 77%

Replicate SD is the spread across the 10 shuffles of one site. The 170 bp effect is stable per site (SD about 0.3); the motif and peak effects scatter more (SD about 0.7 and 0.6). The median over thousands of sites is precise, but an individual site's peak-shuffle value should not be interpreted on its own. This is why 10 replicates were kept.

9. What to trust

ClaimVerdictEvidence
Shuffling the 170 bp around a site removes far more predicted accessibility than shuffling the 11 bp motif alone✓ RobustMedian log2FC -1.75 (170 bp shuffle) vs -0.61 (motif shuffle) in Stable sites; 94% of sites show a 170 bp effect beyond 2 standard errors of their own replicate scatter.
Stable sites depend more on their 170 bp neighbourhood than Dynamic sites do✓ RobustDifference of medians +0.52 (95% CI +0.41 to +0.62), FDR 1.5e-34, permutation p = 0.0002. Holds in every native-accessibility quintile (all five FDR < 0.05), after adjusting for native ATAC and peak width (adjusted differences +0.46 to +0.61, all ***), and in every dynamic class. Direction replicates with the independent Patski ATAC track but is smaller (+0.16, **).
The direction of change (age up vs down, exercise up vs down) changes how much a site depends on its sequence✗ Not supportedDirectly comparing Age Up vs Age Down, and Exercise Up vs Exercise Down, shows no significant difference at 170 bp or peak level (smallest FDR 0.13). The large effects are all 'stably bound vs not', not up vs down.
Dynamic sites lose less accessibility than Stable sites when the whole peak is shuffled~ Plausible / partialRaw difference +0.19 (***), but small (Cliff's delta 0.10) and it mostly disappears after adjusting for native ATAC and peak width (adjusted +0.02 to +0.11; 1 of 6 class contrasts still FDR < 0.05). Not reproduced with the Patski track. Treat as a peak-width/accessibility effect.
Motif-only shuffling differs between Stable and Dynamic sites✗ Not supportedDifference +0.06 (Cliff's delta 0.05, negligible); permutation p = 0.091; not reproduced with the Patski track. A few individual classes (Age Down, Exercise Up, YS only, MAE only) differ by about 0.15 to 0.26 after adjustment, which is small relative to the replicate scatter.
Predicted RNA changes when an AP-1 site or peak is shuffled✗ Not supportedMedian RNA effects are about 0 (|log2FC| mostly < 0.1; largest -0.07 within 2 kb of a TSS). ATAC and RNA effects are correlated across sites (rho 0.19 to 0.24) but the RNA effect itself is tiny. Not informative with these tracks.
Predicted accessibility tracks measured snATAC accessibility~ Plausible / partialSpearman rho 0.40 (n = 3365) for the peak readout; lower for 170 bp and motif readouts. Good enough to be informative, not a precise predictor.
In a peak swap, the swapped-in sequence (not the location) sets accessibility✓ RobustSwapped vs donor native rho 0.75; vs recipient native 0.36. Caveat: only 4 recipients, so the 292 pairs are not independent (about 73 independent donors).
Inserting an AP-1 motif into a shuffled random background raises accessibility✗ Not supported+0.10 log2FC at the centre (p = 0.43); background ATAC is near zero, so the readout is at the floor. No usable signal.
Fibroblast results; MPRA agreement? Cannot judge yetFibroblast-site shuffles and the MPRA run are not finished at the time of this report. The fibroblast tracks available in the mouse model (Patski, embryonic fibroblast RNA) validated weakly against measured accessibility.

10. Open issues and next steps

  • Site set vs the slides. The TOBIAS table gives 3,679 CM Fos sites (2,907 Stable), not the slides' 2,663 (2,320 Stable). Our Dynamic native accessibility matches the slides, but our Stable sites are about half as accessible on average, and keeping our top 80% by predicted accessibility does not close the gap. The slides' Stable sites are a different set. Until the original selection is known, compare patterns, not absolute values.
  • Model equivalence. The slides were made with the AlphaGenome API; this run uses the PyTorch port with the same family of weights. The Dynamic-site match supports equivalence, but a direct check on the same sites through the API would settle it.
  • Fibroblasts. The mouse model has no fibroblast ATAC; Patski and embryonic-fibroblast RNA are weak proxies. The fibroblast shuffle run and the MPRA comparison will be added when they finish.
  • Motif-width effect is larger than in the slides (about -0.6 vs -0.12). Candidate causes are the motif interval used (here the 11 bp TOBIAS interval for both the shuffle and the readout) and the different Stable set; worth confirming the slides' definition.
Methods and files

Predictions: alphagenome-pytorch with model_all_folds weights, mouse organism, 131,072 bp window centred on the motif midpoint, mouse heart ATAC track (1 bp, mean over region), 10 uniform random shuffles per width. Stable = bound in YS, MAS and MAE; age class compares YS and MAS; exercise class compares MAS and MAE. Adjusted model: effect ~ class + log10(native ATAC over peak) + log10(peak width), HC3 robust SEs, normal-theory CIs. All CIs for medians are percentile bootstrap (1,000–2,000 resamples). Sites are treated as independent, but about 8% of sites share a peak with another site, so p-values are mildly optimistic; effect sizes and confidence intervals are the better guide. Tables: Analysis/cm/tables, Analysis/cm/stats; figures: Analysis/cm/figures; scripts: Scripts/22_shuffle_analysis.py, 24_class_stats.py, 23_insertion_analysis.py, 25_build_report.py.
